newsitem.title: FRANCE: FRENCH BILLBOARD FIRMS RUN "GOOD GUYS" CAMPAIGN.
newsitem.headline: FRENCH BILLBOARD FIRMS RUN "GOOD GUYS" CAMPAIGN.

text.p: France's billboard firms are using the slogan "Freedom of speech began on walls" for a campaign aimed at portraying themselves as good guys.
The campaign was devised by advertising agency Alice, part of Interpublic Group's Lowe Group, for the billboard owners' association, Union de la Publicite Exterieur (UPE).
The campaign aims to highlight for the first time the billboard firms' role in giving free space to charities and good causes, an Alice executive said on Friday.
The campaign was launched on July 20 with two posters, each emblazoned with the free speech slogan.
One poster is a reproduction of a 22,000 year-old human hand-print from a cave wall in southern France, the earliest known wall painting.

The other is a photograph of an erotic mosaic on the wall of a house which survived the destruction of Pompeii when the volcano Vesuvius erupted. The mosaic was chosen to illustrate the sexual licence of Pompeii at the time, the Alice executive said.
Starting in the autumn, each time UPE billboards are used for a charitable campaign, the free speech slogan and a reduced version of one of the two posters will be carried as well, he said.
"We wanted to show with this campaign... that poster advertising has a real social use," he said.
UPE has donated its billboards to good causes and charities for a long time, but no one knows it does so, the Alice executive said.
The poster campaign will run through the summer holidays using UPE members' vacant billboard space.
